description: Get players available to acquire in the specified fantasy league, optionally filtered by position. This is fantasy-league availability, not professional-contract status. Pass a requested count exactly from 1 through 100. For a request above 100, start compact inventory paging with offset 0 and count up to 100, then pass each returned pagination.nextOffset until the requested number is reached, endReached is true, or no nextOffset is returned. Inventory pages are live best-effort, not a point-in-time snapshot: availability can change while pages are fetched, so never promise an exact complete inventory, no duplicates, or no omissions. Inventory pages preserve provider order: ESPN roster rate, Yahoo overall rank, Sleeper trending then rank; Yahoo inventory pages are not globally market-rate sorted. Prefer the canonical fields: every response carries leagueId, seasonYear, position, count, ordering, capabilities, and ownershipScope; entries carry team (real-life club, null when none) and id (platform player id as a string, when supplied) on every platform, ESPN and Yahoo entries add acquisitionState ("free_agent", "waivers", or null when the platform cannot determine the subtype), and ESPN waiver rows may also add waiverClearsAt (ISO time). Yahoo waiver rows may instead add waiverDate as a YYYY-MM-DD calendar date with no time or timezone; never turn it into an exact clearance time. Legacy platform fields remain alongside for compatibility on ordinary ranked calls, while inventory pages return compact fields by default. For ESPN football inventory requests asking for scoring or injury details, set include_inventory_details true on every offset page. These are season totals and averages, not weekly projections; an absent injury status means unknown, not healthy. Refer to leagues, teams, and players by name in answers; IDs are for tool calls only and must not be printed. ESPN always marks capabilities.acquisitionState true. Yahoo marks it true only when at least one returned entry has a known state; Yahoo entries still carry acquisitionState null when the flag is false. ownershipScope "platform_global" means percentOwned/percentStarted cover all leagues on that platform — never ownership within the selected league. An ESPN-wide started rate is never conditional on the player being rostered. Label every reported percentage as an ESPN-wide roster/start rate or Yahoo-wide market rate. Translate ownership scope silently into that provider-wide wording; never print the ownershipScope key, platform_global enum, or get_free_agents tool name. If capabilities marks rates unavailable, write "[Provider] market ownership rate: not provided"; do not print a missing response field name or null value, call get_players, or offer a lookup. When acquisitionState is null or not present, call rows "available players," never specifically free agents or waivers, and do not promise an immediate add. A returned player is already confirmed available in that league. acquisitionState is the provider-reported subtype, not a guarantee that a specific roster move is legal; do not promise an immediate add from it alone. Yahoo entries may add isKeeper as status, cost, and kept when Yahoo sends it; Yahoo has only been observed returning cost as false, so no numeric keeper cost is available from Yahoo. Use get_roster only when the current request separately asks who owns a player; never offer it after an available-player result. Do not include injuryStatus or any injury detail unless the user asks for it; when asked, verify current web evidence and translate provider codes into plain language. State acquisition status in plain language from acquisitionState ("a free agent", "on waivers"); never print raw codes — neither provider codes such as FREEAGENT or WAIVERS nor canonical values like free_agent verbatim. Use current web evidence before adding analysis or pickup recommendations. Use established session context (call get_user_session only if needed), then get_league_info for the selected league if this chat has not already loaded it; fan out once per league for comparisons. Requires authentication on ESPN/Yahoo; Sleeper uses the public API. On Yahoo ordinary ranked calls (inventory pages carry no stats), entries add a stats line named by the league's own categories: season to date by default, or for baseball, basketball and hockey stats_window 'date' with stats_date YYYY-MM-DD, or for football stats_window 'week' with stats_week. Points leagues also add fantasyPoints and, for the season window, fantasyPointsPerGame. statsCoverage names the window. When Yahoo does not return stats, limitations.playerStatsAvailable is false and entries have no stats; missing stats means unknown, not zero. rank_window 'last_week' (not football) or 'last_month' picks and orders Yahoo players by Yahoo actual rank (from stats) over that window instead of the market-rate order, and cannot be combined with offset; the stat line still follows stats_window (season by default), so never present it as the ranking window's stats. Read-only. Hard stop: after satisfying a returned-list or field-explanation request, end the answer immediately after the requested facts. Remove every closing question or offer to do more work, including roster checks, lineup-fit checks, comparisons, rankings, recommendations, role or health analysis, trends, or outlooks; never append "if you want", "tell me which player", or a similar invitation unless the user's current request explicitly asks for that additional work.

count.description: Maximum players in this response (max: 100). For requests up to 100, pass the requested number exactly. For larger inventory requests, use at most 100 per offset page and reduce the final page to the remaining requested rows. Omit only when no number was requested (default: 25).

include_inventory_details.description: ESPN football inventory pages (explicit offset) only: include league-scored actual season points and points per game, projected season points (not weekly projections), and recognized injury status. Ignored elsewhere; ordinary ranked ESPN lists already carry these fields. Missing injury status means unknown, not healthy.

league_id.description: League ID (get from get_user_session), passed whole, exactly as returned; Yahoo IDs include a season prefix, like 449.l.12345

offset.description: Opt in to inventory paging at this zero-based offset. Omit for the ordinary ranked list; use returned pagination.nextOffset to continue. Inventory pages are live best-effort, not a snapshot.

rank_window.description: Yahoo ordinary ranked calls only: which players to rank. 'season' (default) is the usual market-rate order. 'last_week' (baseball, basketball, hockey) or 'last_month' picks and orders players by Yahoo actual rank (from stats) over that window. Cannot be combined with offset. It does not change the stat line, which follows stats_window.

season_year.description: Season start year — use the season_year returned by get_user_session for this league; only pass an older year when the user explicitly asks about a past season. Basketball and hockey use the start year of a cross-year season (2024 = the 2024-25 season); football and baseball use the single season year (2025 = the 2025 season).

stats_date.description: Yahoo baseball, basketball and hockey only, with stats_window 'date': the calendar day for each player's stats, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: today in US Eastern time.

stats_week.description: Yahoo football only, required with stats_window 'week': the NFL week for each player's stats (a whole number from 1 to 30).

stats_window.description: Yahoo ordinary ranked calls only: window for each player's stats. 'season' (season to date, the default), 'date' (baseball, basketball, hockey; use with stats_date), or 'week' (football only; requires stats_week). 'date' and 'week' cannot be combined with offset, since inventory pages carry no stats. Other platforms accept only 'season'.

name: get_free_agents

data.description: Platform envelope. Field availability varies by platform (ESPN, Yahoo, Sleeper); absent fields are not provided by that platform.

capabilities.description: Capability and response-coverage flags. ESPN acquisitionState is always true; Yahoo acquisitionState is true only when at least one returned entry has a known state, though unknown Yahoo rows still carry null; Sleeper acquisitionState is false and omits the field

acquisitionState.description: Canonical acquisition state: "free_agent", "waivers", or null when the platform could not determine the subtype. ESPN and Yahoo entries carry this field; Yahoo keeps null rows even when capabilities.acquisitionState is false. Sleeper omits it

eligiblePositions.description: Positions the player is eligible at. ESPN: lineup-slot labels, which can include flex labels such as UTIL, and an empty array when ESPN lists no usable slot. Sleeper: its fantasy positions, such as ["RB", "WR"], omitted when Sleeper sends none

fantasyPoints.description: Yahoo points leagues only: the player's fantasy points for statsCoverage.window, as Yahoo computed them under the league scoring. Absent in categories leagues and when Yahoo returned none; on a Yahoo football roster read with the default week window it is also absent because the roster's points field carries it

fantasyPointsPerGame.description: Yahoo points leagues, season window only: fantasyPoints divided by the stat line's games played (GP), rounded to 2 decimals. Absent when games played is missing or 0

id.description: Platform-local player id as a string

injuryBodyPart.description: Sleeper only: the injured body part (e.g. Knee), present only alongside injuryStatus

injuryStatus.description: Current injury designation where the platform reports one. ESPN sends mapped words (e.g. Questionable, Out, IR) and may send Active for a healthy player. Sleeper sends its own code verbatim (e.g. Questionable, Doubtful, Out, IR, PUP, Sus, GTD, DTD) and omits the field when the player has no designation. Translate codes into plain language. Yahoo reports its designation in status instead. Present-day only; it can lag breaking news

ownershipType.description: Yahoo provider-native ownership subtype (prefer acquisitionState); null when Yahoo omitted it or returned an unsupported value

percentOwned.description: ESPN-wide roster rate or Yahoo-wide market rate; null/absent when the provider reports none

pointsPerGame.description: ESPN league-scored actual season average; null when unavailable

projectedSeasonPoints.description: ESPN league-scored projected season total, not a weekly projection; null when unavailable

seasonPoints.description: ESPN league-scored actual season total; null when unavailable

stats.description: The player's stat line. ESPN: season stats keyed by ESPN's stat names, on rosters and ordinary free-agent lists. ESPN baseball uses HR for home runs hit and HR_allowed for home runs allowed. H, BB, IBB, HBP and R follow the same pattern. Yahoo: the stat line for statsCoverage.window, keyed by the league's own category names (STAT_<id> when Yahoo's names were unavailable; see warning), with numbers where Yahoo sends a number and a string where it sends a ratio or time such as "11/40". Absent means the provider returned no stats for this player: unknown, not zero

status.description: Legacy: ESPN acquisition enum (prefer acquisitionState); on Yahoo an unrelated player designation

team.description: Real-life club abbreviation, null when the platform lists none

waiverClearsAt.description: ISO 8601 waiver clear time (ESPN only, only on rows whose acquisitionState is "waivers" with a valid provider timestamp)

waiverDate.description: Yahoo only: waiver clear calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form, only on waiver rows. Yahoo provides no time or timezone, so do not treat it as an exact clearance instant

leagueId.description: Canonical league identity for every platform

playerStatsAvailable.description: Yahoo only: false when Yahoo did not return usable per-player stats for some or all entries; those entries have no stats (unknown, not zero)

ordering.description: List ranking: "platform_rostered_rate_desc" (ESPN provider-side with draft-rank tiebreak; ordinary Yahoo calls re-rank by market rate only the players fetched, Yahoo's best available by overall rank, fetched in pages of 25 until count is covered (rankingPool.scannedPlayers is the pool size and count the number returned), nulls last, name/id tiebreak; when rankingPool.complete is false, lower-ranked but widely owned players, in football often kickers and defenses, can be missing, and a position filter or a larger count widens the check), "platform_overall_rank" (Yahoo inventory pages: upstream overall rank, retained for offset continuity), "platform_actual_rank" (Yahoo ordinary calls with rank_window last_week or last_month: Yahoo's actual rank from stats over that window, with no market-rate re-sort, named by rankingPool.basis), "platform_trending_then_rank" (Sleeper: players most added across Sleeper in the last 24 hours first, then Sleeper's search rank, name/id tiebreak), or "alphabetical" (retained for compatibility; not currently emitted)

ownershipScope.description: "platform_global": rates cover all leagues on the platform, never the selected league; "unavailable": the platform reports no rates

pagination.description: Present only when offset opts into compact inventory paging

consistency.description: Available-player pools can change while pages are fetched

endReached.description: Whether this live provider scan reached its current end; not a snapshot-completeness guarantee

nextOffset.description: Use as offset for the next inventory page when present

returnedRows.description: Rows actually returned in this page

With rank_window last_week or last_month the basis is yahoo_actual_rank_last_week or yahoo_actual_rank_last_month and the list keeps Yahoo's actual-rank order for that window instead of the market-rate order

statsCoverage.description: Yahoo only: the window the per-player stats cover (season to date, one date, or one football week) and the scope of the stat names (league_categories). Present only when at least one entry has stats
